layout_note: Single column, front-matter opening leaf of the 1582 Rhemes NT (scan S8). NOTE ON PAGE POINTER: the task said render page 2, but on the S8 scan raster-index 2 is 'THE PREFACE TO THE READER'; the Censure & Approbation is at raster-index 1 (found by paging; heading + content confirm). Layout top-to-bottom: (1) two-line centred roman-capital display heading 'THE CENSVRE AND / APPROBATION.'; (2) the Latin approbation paragraph set in upright ROMAN type, opened by a decorated woodcut drop-cap 'C' (~3 lines deep) reading 'CVM huius verſionis...'; (3) four signatory blocks, each = a name in roman CAPITALS followed by an office/title description in ITALIC (the Rheims chapter doctors); (4) a roman citation line 'S. Auguſt. lib. 1. c. 3. de ſerm. Do. in monte.'; (5) a smaller ROMAN Latin quotation of Augustine; (6) an ITALIC English translation of that quotation; (7) catchword 'THE' at foot-right (anticipates the next leaf 'THE PREFACE...'). No running header; no printed folio or quire-signature visible on this leaf. GLYPH REGIMES: Latin body + Augustine quote are roman (real w-fount, but NO w-sorts occur in the Latin); italic office-descriptions use real w (none occur); the small ITALIC English translation is apparatus type that sets w as gapped 'vv' (Vve, vvhere, ſhevv) and s as long-ſ. This leaf was captured at LOW native resolution (741x966 px, ~138 DPI equiv; jp2 file only 106 KB vs ~1.6 MB for the hi-res leaves in the same S8 set), which caps confidence on a few fine italic terminals and one minim cluster (see uncertain).

cogniti, aliiíque S. Theologiæ & linguæ

_revises_review.evidence: Measured on M, not judged by eye. In the band above x-height the word carries FOUR marks: the l-ascender (x56-67, rows 0-26), TWO round dots (x86-93 and x110-117, both rows 5-12, w=8), and a larger slanted mark (x140-152, rows 1-19, w=13) -- an acute, not a dot. The acute stands one full letter-pitch (24px, matching the dot-to-dot spacing) beyond the second dot, so it sits over a THIRD minim. The x-height stroke groups agree: a / l / i / i / [i+q merged] / u / e.
_revises_review.reading: THREE i-letters, the third carrying the acute of the enclitic -que. Standard Latin is 'aliíque' (alii + -que); the extra minim is the compositor's dittography and is preserved as printed, per GUIDELINES 'preserve typos'.
_revises_review.STATUS: OPEN FOR SIR. This revises a correction Sir APPLIED on 2026-07-23. That correction was made on the 138-dpi X substitute, where two minims and an acute are not separable; it is not being overruled on judgement but re-taken on an image 3.4x better. Flagged rather than silently changed.

uncertain.note: Both terminal -æ endings are set with the e-caudata (ę, U+0119), NOT the æ ligature — diplomatically preserved as printed ('Catholicę', 'Eccleſię'). High confidence on the caudata form. 'Eccleſię' read with a long-ſ (roman body); medium confidence on the exact s-form vs round-s at this resolution.

Set with the æ ligature. A faint mark over the æ suggests the same enclitic acute clearly seen on 'aliíque' (i.e. 'vitǽque', U+01FD). Too faint to confirm at ~138 DPI; transcribed plain 'vitæque' and flagged rather than adding an unconfirmed diacritic.

Italic terminal æ is faint at native resolution and could read 'a'. The fount's æ is otherwise visible elsewhere in the same italic (Eccleſiæ, Academiæ, Theologiæ); grammar (genitive agreeing with 'inſignis Eccleſiæ') and the known text give 'Metropolitanæ'. Medium confidence.

Numeral after 'lib.' transcribed as Arabic '1' (book 1 of Augustine, De sermone Domini in monte — the 'beati pauperes spiritu' chapter, cap. 3, matching 'c. 3.'). The single-stroke glyph could alternatively be read 'i/j'; Arabic '1' chosen for consistency with the Arabic 'c. 3.'

glyph_counts.note: Hand estimate over the whole leaf (Latin roman paragraph + italic signatory offices + Augustine roman quote + italic English translation). Subject to script recompute; the transcription text is the source of truth. Includes double long-ſſ in 'poſſe' and 'profeſſor'.

sfoot_glyphs.note: Latin has no w-sorts. The gapped 'vv' occurs ONLY in the small italic English-translation apparatus (Vve / vvhere / ſhevv) — kept as vv per §w-regime (italic apparatus). Body/roman regime would be real 'w' but no w-words appear.

method: Re-read from NT-1582-M's own raster (embedded CCITT stencil pulled from S06.pdf via witness/extract_pdf_leaves.py, polarity normalised by minority-class). Read in 7 overlapping horizontal bands at 0.64x, then targeted crops at 3-4x for the w-regime capitals and the two diacritic questions, plus objective connected-component counts in the diacritic band for the minim call. Zoom held at or below 4x: past ~5x a bitonal sort pixelates and proves nothing.
confidence: High on the display heading, the roman approbation paragraph, the four signatory names, and the Augustine Latin quote + italic English translation. Medium on a few faint italic terminals (Metropolitanæ æ, Eccleſię s-form) and the e-caudata calls. Specifically flagged: the 'aliíque' minim count (2 vs 3), the possible 'vitǽque' enclitic acute, and the 'lib. 1.' numeral. Overall very-high textual confidence but capped below the S1/S8 hi-res leaves by this leaf's low native raster (741x966, ~138 DPI).
glyph_regime_resolved: Two regimes on one leaf. (A) Roman/upright: the approbation paragraph, the Augustine citation line, and the Augustine Latin quotation — real-w fount but NO w-sorts occur; long-ſ per glyph; ct/ſt ligatures transcribed as component letters (Doctor, poteſtati, iſta, Auguſt.); e-caudata ę for -æ endings (Catholicę, Eccleſię); macron abbreviation Scripturarū = Scripturarum; u/v and i/j period-swaps preserved (verſionis, vllo, ciuili, promouere, vtiliter, Iuris, Collegij). (B) Italic: signatory office descriptions (real-w fount, no w-words), and the small English translation which is APPARATUS type setting w as gapped 'vv' (Vve, vvhere, ſhevv) and s as long-ſ — vv kept per §w-regime. Ampersands transcribed '&' in both regimes.

resolved_uncertain.note: An acute accent is clearly present marking the enclitic -que (compositor's practice in this text). At the low native resolution the minim cluster is ambiguous between two i-strokes (aliíque, = alii + -que; standard text and grammar, nom. pl. agreeing with 'viri conteſtati ſint') and an apparent third minim (aliiíque). Transcribed 'aliíque' (the lexically-sound reading); flagged rather than inventing a nonstandard triple-i from sub-resolution evidence. No long-ſ here (no s in the word).

_prior_provenance.note: Read from NT-1582-X (S08) raster-index 1 at 138 dpi. That leaf is one of X's TWO MADE-UP leaves -- a low-resolution substitute spliced in from another copy (~771x1103, mode-L, against 5000-6000px RGB for X's other 798 leaves). Its SETTING is correct and is the 1582 one; its RASTER is the worst in the corpus for this leaf.

regrounded.supplying_copy: NT-1582-M -- the NT half of the 2007 Maximus Scriptorius reprint (S06), whose photographs are of an original 1582 Rheims Fogny copy.
regrounded.why: X's leaf and M's leaf are the SAME SETTING (block-registered NCC +0.424 on the matching pair against 0.000-0.036 on every cross-pairing), and M carries it at 2617x4149 against X's ~771x1103 -- about 3.4x linear. This is not a new witness to a new text; it is the same reading at a raster that can actually be read.
regrounded.LIMITING FACTOR: M's raster is 1-BIT CCITT at ~380 ppi, letter-size re-lay-out, ABBYY-processed, from a 2007 print-on-demand reproduction. There is NO continuous-tone original to acquire -- the tone was discarded before the file we hold existed. Every reading below is taken at that ceiling and must be cited with it. It is sufficient for letter identity and for diacritics at 4x; it is NOT training data and NOT CER-evaluation data.
regrounded.still_the_only_source: The base exemplar NT-1582-B lacks this leaf outright. M and X are the only copies of it in the 1582 setting, and X's is a spliced substitute. No genuine alternative exists to check against.
